title: The AND of Every Number in a Range

concept.title: The AND of a range is the common binary prefix of its ends, followed by zeros
body: For each question `l r`, compute the **bitwise AND of all the integers from `l` to `r`** (both included). For `5 7` it is `5 & 6 & 7 = 4`. For `26 30` it is 24. Running the loop is impossible when the range holds 10^18 numbers.

Look at the binary notations of `l` and `r`. As the numbers run from `l` up to `r`, a bit position that is **not** in the common prefix of `l` and `r` takes both values 0 and 1 somewhere in the range, because counting up must pass the place where the first differing bit flips (and when it flips from 0 to 1, all lower bits are 0 at that moment, and just before it they were all 1). So every bit **after** the common prefix is 0 in the AND. Bits of the common prefix are the same in all numbers of the range, so they stay.

body.code:
shift = 0
while l != r:                # remove the bits below the common prefix
    l >>= 1
    r >>= 1
    shift += 1
answer = l << shift          # the common prefix, followed by `shift` zeros

body: The loop runs at most 60 times for each question. For `26 = 11010` and `30 = 11110` the common prefix is `11`, `shift = 3`, and the answer is `11000 = 24`. If `l = r`, the loop does not run and the answer is `l`. The idea of "shift both ends until they meet" is a standard way to find the common prefix without bit-by-bit comparisons.

statement: For each question with two numbers `l` and `r` (`l <= r`) print the bitwise AND of all integers from `l` to `r`, both ends included.
inputFormat: The first line has `q`: the number of questions.
Each of the next `q` lines has two numbers `l` and `r`.
outputFormat: Print `q` numbers on one line, separated by spaces.
hints: Write both ends in binary and look at their common prefix.
Bits after the common prefix become 0.
Shift both numbers right until they are equal, remembering how many shifts were made.

input = sys.stdin.readline

q = int(input())
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

explanation: Both ends are shifted right until they are equal; the common value shifted back left by the number of shifts is the AND of the whole range.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

q = int(input())
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

out = []
for l, rr in qs:
    shift = 0
    while l != rr:
        l >>= 1
        rr >>= 1
        shift += 1
    out.append(l << shift)
print(*out)
